the LMC H1 ridge is a region of collision between two different gas streams from the LMC and SMC, which are likely to have different metallicities.

we have successfully identified the inflow gas of the SMC in the LMC, and the inflow gas has a low dust/gas ratio and low CO-to-H2conversion factor, suggesting that it has low metallicity gas.
the LMC H i ridge region is a good laboratory for studying the interaction between galaxies and/or the collision between the gas components.
the LMC H i ridge region is an interesting site to study the interstellar medium (ISM) in the low-metallicity environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful treatment of the gas component is necessary to understand the gas properties of a star forming region.
the dust/gas ratio is not a good indicator of the metallicity of the ISM.
the gas in this region is not homogeneous, and it is necessary to take into account the inhomogeneity in the study of the star formation in the LMC.
